title: A rejected Engram verification record keeps only the error code; the host drops Engram's refusal message
outcome: When Engram definitively refuses a verification record, the run's retained record keeps Engram's bounded, redacted refusal reason as well as its code, so the refusal can be diagnosed without querying live stores or re-running tests.
acceptance: The definite-remote-refusal branch (src/engram_verification_record.rs around lines 1265–1276 at 47fdba2f) records the refusal code plus Engram's bounded refusal message and any structured reason fields, with a size limit and with secrets excluded.
A regression test drives a definite refusal carrying a message and asserts that the retained rejected detail includes the bounded message, and the review pair is clean.
